title: Microservices Patterns & Distributed Resilience
description: Master Circuit Breakers, the CAP Theorem, CQRS, and resilient saga orchestration.

questions.question: Which design pattern stops cascaded failures across distributed microservices by failing fast when a dependency is down?
options: Circuit Breaker Pattern
Singleton Pattern
Factory Method Pattern
Observer Pattern

questions.question: What does the CAP theorem state regarding distributed data stores?
options: A distributed system can guarantee at most two out of Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance
All distributed nodes must share the exact same physical clock
Compute capacity must always exceed storage capacity by a factor of two
Caches must always invalidate data after 60 seconds

questions.question: Which architecture pattern separates read operations from update operations to optimize performance and security?
options: CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)
Model-View-Controller (MVC)
Layered Monolith
Client-Server Polling

questions.question: In distributed transactions, how does the Saga Pattern manage failure without two-phase commit (2PC)?
options: By executing compensating transactions in reverse order when any local transaction fails
By locking all tables across all databases until every microservice completes
By throwing an unhandled exception and discarding all database records
By restarting all microservice containers automatically

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Strangler Fig pattern?
options: Incrementally replacing legacy monolithic systems by routing functionality to new microservices until the monolith is retired
Compressing CSS bundles to reduce initial page load latency
Killing rogue threads that consume more than 80% CPU
Encrypting hard disk sectors with multi-key derivation
